facts.statement: The genus Galeamopus was established by Tschopp and colleagues in 2015.
facts.quote: authority: Tschopp et al., 2015

facts.statement: Galeamopus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 million years ago, in the lower Morrison Formation of Wyoming.
facts.quote: known from the Late Jurassic lower Morrison Formation (Kimmeridgian age, about 155 million years ago) of Wyoming, United States

facts.statement: The first fossil specimen attributed to Galeamopus was collected by Marshall P. Felch in September 1884 at Garden Park, Colorado.
facts.quote: The first specimen referred to Galeamopus was collected by Marshall P. Felch in September, 1884 at his quarry in Garden Park, Colorado.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Galeamopus was discovered by William H. Utterback in 1902 near Sheridan, Wyoming.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Galeamopus was discovered by fossil hunter William H. Utterback in 1902 near Sheridan, Wyoming

facts.statement: Emanuel Tschopp, Octávio Mateus, and Roger Benson renamed the genus Galeamopus in 2015.
facts.quote: In 2015, it was renamed as the separate genus Galeamopus by Emanuel Tschopp, Octávio Mateus and Roger Benson.

facts.statement: The name Galeamopus means "helmet need" in Latin, referring to the fragile braincase of the type specimen.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin galeam, the accusative of galea, "helmet", and opus, "need".

facts.statement: The genus name is a pun on the first names of discoverers William Utterback and William Holland, translating to "want helmet".
facts.quote: The combination is intended as a translation of Wil-helm, literally "want helmet", in reference to the first name of both Utterback and Holland.

facts.statement: Researchers identified six unique anatomical traits specific to the species Galeamopus hayi.
facts.quote: The study also determined six autapomorphies of the type species Galeamopus hayi alone.

facts.statement: The genus is defined by thirteen unique anatomical features, which researchers deemed enough to justify its separation from other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Combined, there are thirteen autapomorphies present in Galeamopus, which Tschopp and colleagues considered sufficient to support a distinct genus.

facts.statement: In Galeamopus, the ulna is at least 76% as long as the humerus.
facts.quote: The ulna of the lower arm is long, with a minimum length equalling 76% of the humerus, upper arm bone, length.

facts.statement: The underside joint surface of the radius is angled at approximately 15 degrees relative to the shaft.
facts.quote: The joint surface at the underside of the radius is bevelled relative to the shaft, at an angle of about 15°.

facts.statement: The top surface of the shinbone (tibia) features a pinched process behind the cnemial crest.
facts.quote: The outer edge of the top surface of the shinbone forms a pinched process, behind the cnemial crest at the front.

facts.statement: Galeamopus is an extinct diplodocid sauropod dinosaur known for having a weak skull.
facts.quote: Galeamopus ("requiere casco" en referencia al débil cráneo) es un género extinto de dinosaurio saurópodo diplodócido

facts.statement: The thirteen unique traits found in Galeamopus represent the exact minimum number used in the study to separate different genera.
facts.quote: Combinadas, hay trece autopomorfias presentes en Galeamopus, exactamente el mínimo que fue usado en el estudio como criterio para separar géneros diferentes.

facts.statement: In 2017, the specimen nicknamed "Max" was designated the type specimen for the second species, Galeamopus pabsti.
facts.quote: In 2017, the "Max" specimen was made the type specimen of a second Galeamopus species, G. pabsti, by Tschopp and Mateus.

facts.statement: The species Galeamopus pabsti was named in honor of Swiss paleontologist Dr. Ben Pabst.
facts.quote: It was named after the Swiss paleontologist Dr. Ben Pabst, who discovered the specimen and helped mount the skeleton at Sauriermuseum Aathal.

facts.statement: The genus was identified from a partial skeleton discovered by William H. Utterback in 1902 near Sheridan, Wyoming.
facts.quote: Galeamopus fue identificado de un esqueleto parcial descubierto por William H. Utterback en 1902 cerca de Sheridan, Wyoming, en la cantera Red Fork Powder River A.

facts.statement: In 1906, William Jacob Holland referred the skeleton to Diplodocus when he described the neurocranium.
facts.quote: En 1906, el esqueleto fue referido a Diplodocus por William Jacob Holland cuando él describió el neurocráneo.

facts.statement: Holland classified the specimen as a new species of Diplodocus, Diplodocus hayi, in 1924.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue clasificado por Holland como una nueva especie de Diplodocus, Diplodocus hayi, en 1924.

facts.statement: In 2015, Emanuel Tschopp, Octávio Mateus, and Roger Benson renamed this species as a separate genus, Galeamopus.
facts.quote: En 2015, esta especie fue renombrada como un género separado, Galeamopus por Emanuel Tschopp, Octávio Mateus y Roger Benson.

facts.statement: The genus name is derived from the Latin term galeam, the accusative of galea, meaning "helmet", and opus, meaning "need".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del término latino galeam, el acusativo de galea, "casco", y opus, "necesitar".

facts.statement: The name also alludes to the fact that the small neurocranium of the holotype needs coverage.
facts.quote: El nombre es además una alusión al hecho de que el pequeño neurocráneo del holotipo necesita de cobertura.

facts.statement: The genus holotype is HMNS 175, previously CM 662, the original skeleton.
facts.quote: El holotipo del género es HMNS 175, previamente CM 662, el esqueleto original.

facts.statement: In 2017, the specimen "Max" was designated as the type specimen for a second species of Galeamopus, G. pabsti, by Tschopp and Mateus.
facts.quote: En 2017, el espécimen "Max" fue designado como el espécimen tipo de una segunda especie de Galeamopus, G. pabsti, por Tschopp y Mateus.

facts.statement: Galeamopus is considered an advanced sauropod placed as a member of the family Diplodocidae, within a clade alongside Diplodocus in the subfamily Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: Galeamopus es considerado un saurópodo avanzado ubicado como miembro de la familia de Diplodocidae, dentro de esta forma un clado junto a Diplodocus dentro de la subfamilia Diplodocinae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Galeamopus is Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Diplodocinae

facts.statement: Galeamopus belongs to the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Family: Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Galeamopus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Galeamopus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype was found in a layer of the lower zone of the Morrison Formation dating to the Kimmeridgian.
facts.quote: Este fue hallado en una capa de la zona inferior de la Formación Morrison que data del Kimmeridgiense.
